name: colonies-03-wcm-rss-leak
title: Inner EcoliWCM RSS leak — localize and fix
description:
Part A enabling-infrastructure study. colonies-02 recorded a single EcoliWCM
growing RSS ~7.7 MB/sim-s on the macOS mini, reaching ~19 GB before first
division and OOM-killing the sequential colony at 27.5 GB (~34 GB at 2 Ray
cells) — which read as an unbounded native leak blocking HPC deployment.

The 2026-07-26 leak hunt corrected that framing: the per-tick growth is
LOCALIZED (per-process RSS attribution on the mini) to the inner WCM's
polypeptide-elongation step (~82%) + mass-listener (~17%). It is not
unbounded. The truly-retained part is small (~0.2 MB/tick, tracemalloc-visible:
scipy LSODA integrator work arrays held per solve); the scary ~1.4 MB/tick is
macOS allocator arena retention of elongation's per-tick numpy working arrays,
a macOS measurement artifact. A faithful Linux (glibc) reproduction grows only
0.017 MB/tick WITHOUT any fix and 0.000 MB/tick WITH periodic malloc_trim(0),
versus ~1.6 MB/tick on the macOS mini — so on the Linux HPC target the colony's
memory is BOUNDED. The leak is now a characterised, Linux-bounded, mitigated
footnote, not an HPC blocker.
conclusion:
Role: Part A enabling infrastructure. This study set out to localize an
apparent unbounded native leak that appeared to block HPC deployment; the
2026-07-26 leak hunt shows the leak is characterised, localized, and
Linux-bounded — a footnote, not the story.

Findings: the per-tick RSS growth is localized to the inner WCM's
polypeptide-elongation step (~82%) + mass-listener (~17%) (F-06, satisfies
leak-localized). The truly-retained part is small (~0.2 MB/tick = scipy LSODA
work arrays); the ~1.4 MB/tick that read as an unbounded native leak on the
macOS mini is allocator arena retention of elongation's per-tick numpy arrays —
a macOS artifact. On the Linux/glibc HPC target the growth is bounded
(0.017 MB/tick unmitigated, 0.000 with periodic malloc_trim(0)), so the
cells-per-node RAM budget is trustworthy. This reconciles F-01/F-02 (real but
minor Python-emitter win) and F-04/F-05 (the "C-level" and "Numba/LLVM"
readings were macOS observations, not the load-bearing per-tick driver).

Gate: passed — the "unbounded native leak" blocker on
colonies-04-hpc-deployment is resolved by localization + Linux boundedness.
Honest caveat: the boundedness is mechanism-validated in a colima glibc
container, NOT yet confirmed by a full-colony end-to-end HPC-node lifetime run;
that in-situ run, plus the optional malloc_trim / scipy-LSODA solver-reuse
optimizations, remain open engineering items rather than gate blockers.

purpose.question:
Where does the RSS growth in a single EcoliWCM come from, and is it bounded
on the Linux HPC target so per-cell RSS budgets are trustworthy? (Answered:
localized to elongation + mass-listener; small real retention is scipy LSODA
work arrays; the rest is macOS arena churn; on Linux/glibc it is bounded.)
purpose.mechanism:
Final (2026-07-26 leak hunt, supersedes the earlier RAMEmitter and
Numba/LLVM hypotheses): per-process RSS attribution on the mini localizes the
per-tick growth to the inner WCM's polypeptide-elongation step (~82%) +
mass-listener (~17%). Two distinct components:
  (1) Real retention ~0.2 MB/tick (tracemalloc-visible): scipy LSODA
      integrator work arrays (scipy/integrate/_ode.py rwork/iwork) held per
      solve, from solve_ivp(method="LSODA") in the equilibrium /
      two-component / tRNA-charging ODEs. Over a ~3000-tick cell cycle that
      is ~0.6 GB/cell — a small, named optimization target (solver reuse /
      method change / periodic trim).
  (2) Allocator arena retention (the scary ~1.4 MB/tick on the macOS mini):
      elongation allocates large per-tick numpy working arrays
      (buildSequences/polymerize, ~1.3 MB) that are freed but macOS does not
      return to the OS, so RSS climbs — invisible to tracemalloc. A macOS
      allocator artifact, not a leak.
An intermediate session claim that "the emitter is 94% of the leak" was a
warm-process measurement artifact and is WRONG; the growth is intrinsic to
comp.run() (elongation).
Mitigation: periodic malloc_trim(0) on the Linux target returns freed arenas
(0.000 MB/tick with, 0.017 without); solver reuse addresses the small real
retention. A bounded per-cell phenotype panel is streamed to zarr by
ColonyPhenotypeRecorder (a process, not an emitter — processes get a cheap
view rather than deep-copying the cells map).
purpose.expected_outcome:
A per-process/tracemalloc profile attributes >=~80% of growth to named sites
(met: elongation ~82% + mass-listener ~17%; real retention = scipy LSODA work
arrays). On the Linux/glibc target RSS is bounded (0.017 MB/tick unmitigated,
0.000 with periodic malloc_trim), versus the macOS-only arena artifact. The
fix does not alter biology (read-only sink / allocator behavior, no feedback
into state). Not yet run: a full-colony end-to-end HPC-node lifetime confirming
the bound in situ.

build_tasks.motivation:
Fixing before localizing risks treating a symptom. colonies-02 proved
the leak is real, emitter- and transport-independent; this pins it to a
site.
build_tasks.action:
Run sims/profile_leak.py: a single EcoliWCM for ~2500 ticks with
tracemalloc snapshots every ~200 ticks, recording top allocation deltas,
gc object-type counts, len(chromosome_history), and inner-composite
state size. Commit profiling/leak_profile.csv + a top-sites table as
evidence. Decide the fix from the data.

build_tasks.motivation: Bounded per-cell RSS is the gate condition for HPC deployment.
build_tasks.action:
Apply the smallest fix the profile justifies (e.g. cap/disable
chromosome_history when unused; release inner-composite per-tick
retention). Keep it behind a flag if it changes recorded outputs.

pipeline_gate.proceed_condition:
Met: the 2026-07-26 hunt localizes >=~80% of the growth to named sites
(elongation ~82% + mass-listener ~17%; real retention = scipy LSODA work
arrays) and shows the growth is Linux-bounded (0.017 MB/tick unmitigated,
0.000 with malloc_trim). Gate proceeds.
pipeline_gate.blocks_until_resolved:
Resolved for HPC purposes: the "unbounded native leak" was substantially a
macOS allocator artifact. On the Linux/glibc HPC target per-cell RSS is
bounded (mechanism-validated in a colima glibc container), so the
cells-per-node budget is trustworthy. colonies-04-hpc-deployment is unblocked;
the remaining open item is a full-colony end-to-end HPC-node run to confirm
the bound in situ (not yet run) plus the optional scipy-LSODA solver-reuse
optimization for the small (~0.2 MB/tick) real retention.

simulation_set.name: profile-1cell-predivision
simulation_set.description:
Single EcoliWCM (no colony/pymunk), ~2500 ticks (pre-first-division),
tracemalloc + gc profiling. Localization run.

simulation_set.name: postfix-seq-1cell-4div
simulation_set.description:
After the fix, re-run colonies-02's sequential natural-division colony
to confirm 3 generations complete without OOM and RSS stays bounded.
(Run via colonies-02 sims/run.py on the fixed branch.)

behavior_tests.name: leak-localized
behavior_tests.description:
A profiling run attributes >=~80% of RSS growth to named sites so a fix is
targeted, not speculative. MET (2026-07-26): per-process RSS attribution
localizes the growth to elongation (~82%) + mass-listener (~17%); the
real-retention component is the scipy LSODA integrator work arrays.

behavior_tests.name: per-cell-rss-bounded-after-fix
behavior_tests.description:
Per-cell RSS is bounded on the Linux HPC target (not the macOS mini, where
freed arenas are retained by the allocator). MET at the mechanism level:
a faithful Linux/glibc reproduction grows 0.017 MB/tick unmitigated and
0.000 MB/tick with periodic malloc_trim(0), versus ~1.6 on the macOS mini.
Validated in a colima glibc container; NOT yet confirmed by a full-colony
end-to-end HPC-node lifetime run.

behavior_tests.name: biology-unchanged-by-fix
behavior_tests.description:
The fix does not alter recorded biology: first division still at tick
2338, per-cell mass at division within RNG of the colonies-02 run.

findings.statement:
The colonies-02 ~7.7 MB/sim-s per-cell RSS leak is the inner per-cell
RAMEmitter, not chromosome_history and not "emitter-independent". Each
embedded cell's inner Composite (built by baseline() in the EcoliWCM
bridge) gets a default RAMEmitter whose no-override branch
(_helpers.py) captures `bulk` (~25k-molecule array) + four unique-
molecule node arrays every tick into an unbounded history list that is
never read. colonies-02's no-emitter probe nulled only the outer colony
emitter, missing the per-cell inner emitters.
findings.evidence:
Live profiler measured the inner RAMEmitter history at ~5.15 MB/row,
growing 1:1 with ticks (9.9 MB @ 2 rows -> 9324 MB @ 1802 rows), tracking
the RSS climb. Confirmed by reading process_bigraph Emitter.inputs() ==
config['emit'] (the emitter only stores its emit_schema ports).

findings.verdict: PASS (single-cell bridge path); multi-cell colony no-OOM = confirmatory follow-up
findings.statement:
Setting the inner RAMEmitter to 'minimal' capture (global_time +
listeners only) for embedded cells bounds per-cell RSS. A single
EcoliWCM built through the bridge (set_ram_emitter_capture('minimal'))
holds RSS essentially flat.
findings.evidence:
Bridge-path profile_leak.py (commit bd1a11fe) RSS: 1.3 GB @ 21 min ->
1.7 GB @ 48 min -> 1.9 GB @ 62 min (~0.25 MB/s, legitimate cell growth),
vs the unfixed path +24 GB by tick 1800 (~7.7 MB/s). ~30x reduction;
no monotonic emitter-driven climb.
findings.next_action:
Confirmatory (not load-bearing): run colonies-02 seq-1cell-4div to full
duration on the mini to show the multi-cell colony completes >=3
generations without OOM. The fix is per-cell, so N bounded cells follow.

findings.statement:
The fix only narrows what the inner RAMEmitter records (a read-only
history sink); the emit_schema does not feed back into simulation state,
so division timing and masses are unchanged by construction. The full
colony re-run (first division still tick 2338) is the empirical
re-confirmation, deferred with the no-OOM run above.

findings.verdict: REFINED by F-06 — C-level growth confirmed, but localized (elongation+mass-listener) and Linux-bounded, not a multi-gen HPC blocker
findings.statement:
The inner-RAMEmitter fix (F-01/F-02) is real and bounds a single bare WCM,
but it is not the dominant leak for a multi-cell colony. Re-running
colonies-02 on current main with all three contributory fixes live
(#239 inner emitter, emit_cells=False outer emitter, viva-munk #11 pymunk
shape churn) still leaks ~0.5-1 MB/tick/cell: the count=6 plateau climbed
5.1 -> 22.3 GB at a constant 6 cells and OOMs ~gen 3, unchanged from before
the fixes.
Refined by the 2026-07-26 leak hunt: the "C-level dominant leak" call stands as a macOS observation but is not an unbounded native leak. Per-process attribution localizes it to elongation (~82%) + mass-listener (~17%); the C-level growth is macOS allocator arena retention of elongation's per-tick numpy arrays plus ~0.2 MB/tick of retained scipy LSODA work arrays. On Linux/glibc it is bounded (0.017 unmitigated, 0.000 with malloc_trim). See F-06.
findings.evidence:
tracemalloc(4) over 150 ticks at 2 forced-division cells: RSS climbed
1396 -> 1586 MB (+1.3 MB/tick), leak reproduced, yet tracemalloc
accounted for only ~1-2 MB of retained Python allocations (largest single
site +0.08 MB; all transient WCM compute: counts_deriver/translation_deriver
np.bincount, scipy-sparse .dot). So the dominant allocator is C-level /
native (numpy/scipy array buffers or a C-extension retaining or fragmenting
memory), invisible to tracemalloc (it tracks only CPython's allocator, not
numpy's). gc object-count scans likewise found only small symptoms
(pymunk Segments -> #11), not the megabytes.
findings.next_action:
Needs a NATIVE heap profiler (macOS `leaks`/`malloc_history` with
MALLOC_STACK_LOGGING, or jemalloc/tcmalloc heap profiling), not Python
tooling. Until then the colony is RAM-blocked for multi-generation runs and
colonies-04-hpc-deployment stays blocked. The 3 Python-level fixes remain
valid wins (merged).

findings.verdict: REFINED by F-06 — LLVM/Numba was a small one-time true-leak signal, not the per-tick driver; per-tick growth is elongation+mass-listener, Linux-bounded (#253 not load-bearing)
findings.statement:
The dominant per-tick growth is native and localized to the LLVM/Numba JIT
layer. A controlled staged run (colonies-02 sims/mem_measure.py) shows
numpy-object bytes flat within each cell-count plateau while native memory
climbs (decomposition figure), and macOS `leaks` (MallocStackLogging) finds
the true unreachable leak with stacks in llvmlite's LLVM pass pipeline
(LLVMPY_buildFunctionSimplificationPipeline). So the WCM's JIT compilation
is the source, not the emitters (#239), the outer emitter (emit_cells), the
pymunk shapes (viva-munk #11), or a retained numpy array.
Refined by the 2026-07-26 leak hunt: the LLVM/Numba JIT stacks that macOS `leaks` surfaced were a one-time/small true-leak signal (~13 MB), not the per-tick driver. The per-tick growth is intrinsic to comp.run() elongation (~82%) + mass-listener (~17%): macOS arena retention of per-tick numpy arrays plus ~0.2 MB/tick of scipy LSODA work arrays. It is Linux-bounded. So #253 (JIT recompilation) is not the load-bearing fix; the actionable targets are periodic malloc_trim(0) and scipy-LSODA solver reuse. See F-06.
findings.evidence:
leaks @2cells/400ticks: ~846 MB live, ~13 MB true leak, top stacks all
LLVM PassBuilder (GVN/JumpThreading/LoopUnswitch/LICM). numpy-bytes delta
~0 within plateaus; tracemalloc <2 MB of a +151 MB/300-tick growth.
Figures: colonies-02 charts/03_memory_decomposition.svg (native vs numpy),
charts/01_rss_vs_tick_by_ncells.svg (per-tick slope by N).
findings.next_action:
Tracked as engineering issue #253: find where the WCM (re)compiles @njit
functions per tick/cell and make them module-level + cache=True so they
compile once and are shared; confirm with NUMBA_DISABLE_JIT=1 flattening the
growth. Separately, the per-cell footprint (each cell = an independent
baseline composite loading its own sim_data, ~1+ GB/cell, colonies-02
charts/02) is a distinct, bounded RAM limiter worth a shared-sim_data design.

findings.statement:
The colony per-tick RSS growth is localized and Linux-bounded, not an
unbounded native leak (this is the corrected diagnosis that reconciles
F-01/F-02/F-04/F-05). Per-process RSS attribution on the mini pins the growth
to the inner WCM's polypeptide-elongation step (~82%) + mass-listener (~17%).
Two components: (1) a small real retention ~0.2 MB/tick (tracemalloc-visible)
= scipy LSODA integrator work arrays (rwork/iwork) held per solve from
solve_ivp(method="LSODA") in the equilibrium / two-component / tRNA-charging
ODEs (~0.6 GB over a ~3000-tick cycle); (2) the scary ~1.4 MB/tick =
macOS allocator arena retention of elongation's large per-tick numpy working
arrays (buildSequences/polymerize, ~1.3 MB), freed but not returned to the OS,
invisible to tracemalloc — a macOS artifact. The earlier "emitter is 94% of
the leak" reading was a warm-process artifact and is wrong.
findings.evidence:
Linux/glibc validation (colima container, faithful reproduction of both
sources): RSS grew 0.017 MB/tick WITHOUT any fix and 0.000 MB/tick WITH
periodic malloc_trim(0), versus ~1.6 MB/tick on the macOS mini. Per-process
attribution: elongation ~82%, mass-listener ~17%. tracemalloc localizes the
~0.2 MB/tick retained component to scipy/integrate/_ode.py work arrays.
findings.next_action:
Two optional, bounded optimizations (neither is an HPC blocker): periodic
malloc_trim(0) on the Linux target to drive residual arena growth to ~0, and
scipy-LSODA solver reuse (or method change) to remove the ~0.2 MB/tick real
retention. Open verification item: a full-colony end-to-end HPC-node lifetime
run to confirm the bound in situ (mechanism-validated in-container so far).

baseline.name: single-ecoliwcm-long
baseline.note:
Profile a SINGLE EcoliWCM over a long pre-division run (~2500s) — no
colony, no pymunk — so the leak is isolated to the inner whole-cell
composite, not the colony wiring. colonies-02 already showed it is
transport- and emitter-independent.
